Subject: Re: Sudden p99 spikes this evening — initial triage notes

Thanks for the traces, Simo. Quick summary of what we see so far:

- Correlation: p99 spikes align with GPU pool scale-up events. When new workers are brought into the pool, the first ~5-8 requests see an extra 600ms-1.8s overhead. After that tail latency drops back to expected ranges.
- Root cause signal: two factors in the warmup path — (1) OS/AMI kernel init + container runtime cold start, (2) model weight population into GPU memory (KV cache priming). Both add up during instance spin-up.
- Not a networking edge issue — client->edge latencies are steady.

I've attached the short trace and the k8s events slice showing node creation + pod scheduling.

Short-term mitigation we can deploy within 2 hours:
- Route AtlasPay traffic to a small warm pool (pre-warmed instances kept idle, ready to serve) to avoid the cold first-requests. This will add cost but should remove the on-scale p99 blips.
- Add a fast-path reply that returns 202 + queued status for requests that hit unprimed instances (fallback) — will need AtlasPay signoff.

Medium-term: we have an infra change to prefetch model weights into a shared pageable memory range on startup so model load latency reduces. That requires a patch and a canary. ETA for canary: ~2 weeks.

I'll start a hotfix playbook and we will enable extra tracing for the next 6 hours. Jordan — can you confirm if AtlasPay wants the warm pool fallback now?

Rishi
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Rishi / Jordan,

We investigated the account-level launch logs and there was an uptick in AMI kernel module initialization time in the us-west-2 region beginning May 20 02:00 UTC following a minor kernel update from the marketplace image you depend on. That can surface as an extra ~300-900ms per instance during first boot.

Recommendations:
- If you rely on rapid scale-up, consider a warm/standby pool of instances or a custom AMI with the kernel change tested and baked.
- We can whitelist expedited provisioning for retries if you open a support plan request; also providing a pre-baked AMI will avoid the on-boot penalty.

Regards,
AWS Support Engineer (Lara Nguyen)
